name: pbtools
baseline: Google Protocol Buffers C++ (libprotobuf 3.6.1) and protobuf-c
workload: Encode and decode of two protobuf messages from Google's benchmark proto ('Message' wrapping Message1 with 566-byte wire size, and Message3 with 106-byte wire size), 2,000,000 iterations each, per library.
claimed_speedup: Encoding: pbtools -O2 1.457 s vs Google protobuf C++ -O3 2.231 s (about 1.53x faster, derived from page data) and vs protobuf-c -O3 1.892 s (about 1.30x, derived from page data). Decoding: pbtools -O2 1.594 s vs Google -O3 1.997 s (about 1.25x, derived from page data) and vs protobuf-c -O3 2.508 s (about 1.57x, derived from page data). With -O2 -flto pbtools encodes in 1.319 s and decodes in 1.239 s. At -Os pbtools is not ahead on encoding (3.398 s vs protobuf-c 1.970 s, Google 3.713 s).
compiler_and_flags: gcc 8.3.0; per-row flags in the README tables: pbtools -O2 / -O2 -flto / -Os / -Os -flto, protobuf-c and Google -O3 / -Os (protobuf-c also -flto); common CFLAGS -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections (benchmark/common.mk)
tradeoffs: Generates C source from proto3 files with a Python generator; no malloc/free, all allocations come from a caller-supplied workspace (arena) that cannot be freed, so repeated-field lengths cannot change after allocation; generates functions instead of tables, so executable size grows faster than table-driven libraries (README: text 17484 B vs nanopb 21256 B for the benchmark program, but growth is steeper); proto3 only, options, services (gRPC), reserved fields and public imports are not implemented; char must be 8 bits.
caveats: Benchmark is first-party and the toolchain is old (gcc 8.3.0, Google protobuf C++ libprotoc 3.6.1, protobuf-c version not stated), so the Google C++ numbers predate current protobuf releases. The README rows list -O3 for Google and protobuf-c, but the committed benchmark/common.mk sets OPT_SPEED = -O2, so the exact flags per row could not be reproduced from the Makefiles alone. The libraries use different memory models: pbtools builds and decodes into a fixed stack workspace with no malloc, protobuf-c mallocs and frees per iteration, Google C++ reuses one message object on decode and serializes to std::string; the encode loops include building the message, so the comparison favours the arena design. The headline win vanishes at -Os (pbtools encode 3.398 s vs protobuf-c 1.970 s). FlatBuffers decodes in 0.100 s (-O2) but only because it decodes lazily and the benchmark uses fields once. Single machine, single run per row, no variance reported, small messages only. The repo's guessed baseline (msgpack) is wrong: msgpack is not in the benchmark. Project has had no commits since 2023-06-04.
